newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Luka sees 96 pretax up but lower dividend.
newsitem.headline: Luka sees 96 pretax up but lower dividend.

text.p: Slovenia's only port Luka Koper said on Friday it expected 1996 pre-tax profit to rise to 1.5 billion tolars ($10.6 million) from 1.0 billion in 1995, but said it would likely slash its dividend payment.
Luka Koper expects the 1996 dividend to fall to around 100 tolars from 202.5 tolars in 1995.
Mirko Pavsic, a member of Luka's management board, told Reuters the port had traffic of some 6.5 million tonnes of cargo this year, unchanged from 1995.
"We expect to increase cargo traffic to seven million tonnes next year on improved services and better logistics support," Pavsic said.
He said Luka expected to raise cargo traffic mainly to and from Slovenia, Austria and Hungary.
In 1995, Slovenia accounted for 37 percent of the port's cargo traffic, while the remaining cargo was in transit.

Luka, which was listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse in November, is 51-percent owned by the state. The city of Koper owns 7.65 percent of its shares, while 41.35 percent are in the hands if domestic individual or corporate investors.
According to the port's regulation, the state has to approve any foreign investors' purchase of Luka's shares.
"So far the government has not decided whether it would approve any foreign buying of Luka's shares," Pavsic said. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
